sources.citation: Decker, Ken et al. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Arum [aab] and Atoro [tdv] Languages of Nasarawa State, Nigeria. JLSR 2021-048. SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mentions Hasha only as a neighbouring language / in classification discussion; nothing on Hasha prosody.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, David Onoja, Innocent Jonah, John Muniru & Samuel Eju. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Hasha (Yashi) [ybj] Language of Nasarawa State, Nigeria, with Notes on Sambe [xab]. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-059. Dallas: SIL International. 51 pp. (Glottolog hh 609566)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 8.2 'Phonetic inventory of Hasha' (pp.16-17) compares consonant/vowel inventories with Blench 2012, notes geminate vowels; Appendix E (p.30): 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' No stress statement.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019/2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, edition IV. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry 172 Hasha.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; entry lists names, location, population, classification (Plateau: Alumic) and sole reference 'Wordlist: Blench (2016)'.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger [with Barau Kato]. 2012. The Hasha [=Yashi] language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment, printout June 11, 2012. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. iv+24 pp. (Glottolog hh 120179; = 'Wordlist: Blench (2016)' in the Atlas of Nigerian Languages)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 Phonology (p.2) gives 8 vowels, consonant chart, and 3.3 Tones: 'Hasha appears to have three level tones, plus a falling tone. In this transcription, the mid tone is left unmarked.' No mention of stress/accent anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent/penult/promin = 0).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 1999 field recordings / any post-2012 revision of 'The Hasha language of Central Nigeria and its affinities' (Atlas cites it as Blench 2016).

sources.note: A later revision of the wordlist ms might expand sec. 3 Phonology; the Internet Archive's index shows only the 2012 printout was ever posted, so any 2016 version is unpublished.
